item.title: 🟠 One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access, Exploits Now Public
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
Security researchers have published a detailed, working exploit for a Linux kernel use-after-free that lets an unprivileged local user escalate to root and break out of a container. item.title: 🔵 TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: Activity Through 2026-06-07, (Mon, Jun 8th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Supply chain risk — audit third-party dependencies and vendor access.

This diary continues the Internet Storm Center&#;x26;#;39;s tracking of the TeamPCP supply chain campaign, first documented in the SANS white paper When the Security Scanner Became the Weapon and most recently in the handler diary Activity Through 2026-05-24. Since that update, the story moved into two new places: the United States government, which formally caught up to the campaign, and the wider population of attackers now wielding the Mini Shai-Hulud framework that TeamPCP open-sourced last month.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 11h ago
